Let
\[
Y_i=(-1)^{X_i}\in\{-1,1\}.
\]
Then \(X_i\) are unbiased and \(6\)-wise independent iff
\[
\mathbb E\prod_{i\in S}Y_i=0
\]
for every nonempty \(S\subseteq\{1,\dots,12\}\) with \(|S|\le 6\).

We want
\[
P(X_1=\cdots=X_{12})=P(Y=(1,\dots,1))+P(Y=(-1,\dots,-1)).
\]

By averaging any feasible distribution over coordinate permutations and global sign flip \(Y\mapsto -Y\), we may assume the distribution only depends on
\[
T=\#\{i:Y_i=-1\},
\]
and is symmetric under \(T\leftrightarrow 12-T\). Let \(r_d\) be the total probability of \(T=d\) or \(T=12-d\), for \(0\le d\le 6\). The desired probability is \(r_0\).

For a vector with exactly \(t\) minus signs,
\[
\sum_{|S|=j}\prod_{i\in S}Y_i=K_j(t),
\]
where \(K_j\) is the binary Krawtchouk polynomial
\[
K_j(t)=\sum_a(-1)^a\binom{t}{a}\binom{12-t}{j-a}.
\]
Since odd moments vanish automatically by sign symmetry, the constraints are
\[
\sum_{d=0}^6 r_dK_2(d)=
\sum_{d=0}^6 r_dK_4(d)=
\sum_{d=0}^6 r_dK_6(d)=0,
\qquad
\sum_{d=0}^6r_d=1.
\]

Now use the dual certificate
\[
F(t)=\frac{13}{3456}
+\frac{43}{20736}K_2(t)
+\frac{11}{10368}K_4(t)
+\frac{5}{13824}K_6(t).
\]
For \(0\le t\le 6\), its values are
\[
F(0)=1,\quad F(1)=\frac{175}{648},\quad F(2)=\frac7{162},\quad
F(3)=0,\quad F(4)=0,\quad F(5)=\frac1{1296},\quad F(6)=0.
\]
Also \(F(12-t)=F(t)\). Hence \(F(t)\ge \mathbf 1_{\{t=0,12\}}\), so for every feasible distribution,
\[
P(Y=\pm(1,\dots,1))\le \mathbb E F(T).
\]
But the \(K_2,K_4,K_6\) expectations are zero, so
\[
\mathbb E F(T)=\frac{13}{3456}.
\]
Thus the desired probability is at most \(13/3456\).

It remains to show this is attainable. Take the symmetric distribution with
\[
r_0=\frac{13}{3456},\qquad
r_3=\frac{11}{54},\qquad
r_4=\frac{33}{128},\qquad
r_6=\frac{77}{144},
\]
and all other \(r_d=0\), distributing uniformly among strings with those weights and their complements. One checks directly that the \(K_2,K_4,K_6\) averages vanish, so the variables are \(6\)-wise independent.

Therefore
\[
\boxed{\frac{13}{3456}}.
\]
